description.value: A PET study comparing resting regional cerebral glucose metabolism in patients with frontotemporal dementia, frontotemporal dementia associated with motor neuron disease, and healthy subjects.

spans.text: Using statistical parametric mapping (SPM96), we compared the metabolic patterns obtained at rest with positron emission tomography in 10 FTD patients and three FTD-MND patients with those obtained from 46 healthy subjects (HS).

spans.text: At a Z score >3.09 (corresponding to P <0.001, Bonferroni corrected for multiple comparisons), relative metabolic impairment in FTD patients as compared to healthy subjects was observed in most regions of the frontal lobes: bilateral anterior cingulate (Brodmann’s areas, BA 24/32), fronto-polar (BA 10), ventrolateral prefrontal (BA 47), dorsolateral prefrontal (BA 8/9/46), ventrolateral premotor (BA 6/44/45) and dorsolateral premotor (BA 6) areas.

value: Relative metabolic impairment in FTD patients as compared to healthy subjects was observed in most regions of the frontal lobes, extending to the anterior temporal lobes and right inferior parietal region; decreased glucose consumption was also highly significant in bilateral putamen.

Our SPM revealed widespread hypometabolism distributed symmetrically in both frontal lobes; to a lesser degree, glucose uptake was also reduced in anterior lateral temporal regions and bilateral putamen. No significant hypometabolism was observed in medial temporal regions.

value: Metabolic impairment in FTD-MND predominated in bilateral anterior cingulate, medial fronto-polar, and orbitofrontal regions, extending bilaterally to dorsolateral prefrontal, dorsolateral premotor, ventrolateral premotor, anterior temporal regions and putamen when uncorrected for multiple comparisons; hypometabolism extended bilaterally into medial temporal regions at P <0.01 uncorrected.

Similar results were found when the metabolic pattern from three FTD-MND patients was compared to that obtained from healthy subjects. However, contrary to FTD, relative hypometabolism was observed bilaterally in medial temporal lobe regions.
